items.title: Tasan clock: county lung-cancer waiting-time tracker with a day-28 alert and a named nurse navigator who acts on it
items.pathway_step: Referral arrival → first visit → treatment decision → first treatment (THL 21/2016 time points)
items.problem: Goal 3's own wording, 'Potilaat pääsevät hoitoon tavoiteaikojen puitteissa' (S p.5), cannot be checked for any county: THL 2017 says national follow-up of cancer patients' access to care 'has been missing', and we found no later public regional series. The only public lung timing is a diagnosis clock for surgical patients in 5 collaborative areas, 2018–mid-2022.
items.action: Week 1: the county extracts referral arrival, first visit, queue date and first treatment for every lung cancer of the last 12 months. That gives the county's own baseline in days 1–30. From week 5 the dates feed the Tasan dashboard weekly. If there is no treatment decision 28 days after referral arrival, an alert goes to the named nurse navigator. The navigator removes the blocker (test booking, result chasing, MDT slot, HUS/OYS slot) and is the single contact for patient and GP. A monthly board view shows % within 42 days, the median per step, and waits for non-pathway patients (to detect crowding out). The clock tells each county whether its problem is speed (→ T1) or who reaches curative treatment (→ T2). DATA-QUALITY TASK (days 1–30): before any baseline is published, check registry completeness against the EHR. In the 2024 report the age-standardised drug-therapy share is implausibly low in Varsinais-Suomi (0.8% men / 1.0% women), Vantaa-Kerava (3.7% / 3.8%) and Keski-Uusimaa (3.5% / 7.3%) vs ~25% nationally. Lapland is also low (10.0% / 15.3%; CIs below the national level). The likely cause is HILMO coding gaps (data team's inference). So the pilot checks drug, curative-RT and MDT codes, and the no-record cases, against the hospital's own records.
items.already_exists: Hospitals hold the dates, and some have coordinators: roadmap 1.2.3 is still at 'survey existing models' (R p.32). What does not exist is a public, comparable, county-level clock for the Goal 3 target. Tasan is that missing public clock, not the first navigator in Finland.

items.title: Close the missing step in Kymenlaakso's lung pathway: week-1 pathway map, then 3-day CT, reflex biomarkers and pre-agreed HUS surgery slots where missing
items.pathway_step: Suspected lung cancer referral → CT/bronchoscopy/biopsy → biomarkers → lung meeting → HUS surgery decision → first treatment
items.problem: Kymenlaakso diagnosed 591 lung cancers in 2019–2023, about 118 a year (csv denominator). Its surgical patients depend on another organisation: the surgery decision and the operation are made at HUS Meilahti in Helsinki (kymenhva.fi). Each hand-off between the Kotka pathway and HUS is a point where days can be lost. The county sits in Etelä-Suomi, the collaborative area with the longest median diagnosis→surgery time (46.0 d). That figure is fragile (see data basis) and is area-level context only, not a Kymenlaakso number. Kymenlaakso's crude curative-record share is 19.3% (CI 16.3–22.7) vs 27.0% nationally. Age-standardised (chart-digitised): men ≈18.0% (14.1–22.8), women ≈22.7% (17.2–29.3). South Karelia is similar (18.9% crude) but smaller.
items.action: Week 1: map the current pathway (CT → bronchoscopy/EBUS/biopsy → pathology → biomarkers → Kymenhva lung meeting → HUS Meilahti surgery decision) using T3's dates. Then close only the step(s) that the map shows are missing, from a fixed menu: CT within 3 working days of referral; one diagnostic day; a reflex biomarker panel ordered by pathology for non-squamous NSCLC; surgical cases sent to HUS within 7 days of the lung meeting, into pre-agreed slots; T3's navigator owns the clock.
items.already_exists: Kymenhva already runs a lung outpatient work-up and a multidisciplinary lung meeting (kymenhva.fi). T1 does not invent a pathway: it closes the missing step that the week-1 map finds.

items.title: Every new Lapland lung cancer reviewed by the existing OYS lung-cancer MDT (by video), plus shared access to curative radiotherapy at OYS (RT referral, travel and accommodation, SBRT/chemoradiation slots)
items.problem: HERO NUMBER (age-standardised, chart-digitised, ±1 pp): curative-treatment share in Lapland ≈16.2% for men (95% CI 12.7–20.4) vs ≈29.8% in Vantaa-Kerava (24.2–36.1); women ≈23.1% (17.9–29.0) vs ≈39.7% (33.1–47.0). The CIs do not overlap in either sex, so age structure does not explain the gap (crude: 18.5% vs 35.6%). Age-standardised SURGERY share for men is the same: Lapland 9.1% (6.0–13.7) vs Vantaa-Kerava 9.0% (5.5–14.1) (2024 report, Taulukko 3.7). So for men the gap is likely in curative radiotherapy. That is the data team's inference: the 2024 report does not separate curative from palliative RT. For women the surgery share also differs (10.4% vs 20.5%). Lapland's radiotherapy is given at OYS in Oulu (lapha.fi), hundreds of kilometres from much of Lapland. Distance worsens outcomes (roadmap p.12–13), and Norwegian data link travel to lower treatment odds.
items.action: Two parts. (1) Review: week-1 audit of which 2025 Lapland lung cancers were discussed at the existing OYS lung-cancer MDT (answers mentor Q4). Then a rule that every new Lapland lung cancer is listed before the treatment-intent decision, with Lapland's clinician on video and ECOG/G8/CFS attached. (2) Curative-RT access (design arm, unpriced; see design): a direct MDT→OYS radiotherapy referral for curative SBRT or chemoradiation, with a reserved weekly slot quota for Lapland patients. Travel (Kela) and patient-hotel accommodation are booked by T3's navigator at the same time, and the decision is not left to the patient alone. Local follow-up is in Rovaniemi.
items.already_exists: Yes. OYS states that the university hospital is responsible for lung-cancer MDTs, surgery and radiotherapy (oys.fi), and Lapland's radiotherapy is given at OYS (lapha.fi). T2 does not create a board: it closes coverage of the existing one to 100% of new Lapland cases, and turns a curative-RT recommendation into a booked slot with travel and accommodation arranged. The registry's 3.0% 'MDT recorded' figure for Lapland is NOT used as proof of a gap: Helsinki shows 0.1%, so it is a recording artefact.

design: Curative-RT access arm (design, UNPRICED, not a KPI or cost line yet): direct MDT→OYS radiotherapy referral for curative SBRT/chemoradiation; a reserved weekly Lapland slot quota; Kela travel and patient-hotel accommodation booked by the T3 navigator. items.target_times_caveat: CAVEAT: the 42-day / 6-week figure is the generic limit in THL Ohjaus 21/2016 §4.1 (referral arrival → first treatment), the reference the strategy names for Goal 3 (S p.5). That PDF is watermarked 'Vanhentunut' (outdated) and has no lung-specific limit. Cancer-specific access times are due 2026–2028 (roadmap 3.1.2, R p.57). Day-28 alert and the 80% target are Tasan design choices, not official targets.
items.kpi_framing: Target-time caveat: the 42-day KPI follows THL Ohjaus 21/2016, which is marked outdated, has no lung-specific limit, and will be replaced by cancer-specific targets due 2026–2028 (roadmap 3.1.2, p.57). The 80% is a Tasan design choice. Lead KPI is MDT coverage (process). The outcome KPI is the age-standardised, sex-specific curative share, with Pohjois-Pohjanmaa as a proposed peer benchmark, not a promised effect. MDT evidence is observational. 'The gap is in curative RT' is an inference.
items.expected_effect: In population registries, MDT-presented lung patients more often receive surgery and guideline-concordant treatment, with lower mortality. These are observational studies, so selection bias is possible.
